title: Anthracycline (doxorubicin) dilated cardiomyopathy: biventricular failure (high RAP + high LVEDP)
vignette: A 68-year-old woman comes to the office due to a month-long history of worsening fatigue, shortness of breath, and dry cough. The patient has symptoms that worsen with exertion and when lying flat. She has had no chest pain, palpitations, or lightheadedness. The patient has a history of hypertension and breast cancer that is in remission after surgery and doxorubicin-based chemotherapy 15 years ago. She does not use tobacco, alcohol, or illicit drugs. Blood pressure is 110/62 mm Hg and pulse is 94/min. Physical examination shows crackles at the lung bases and bilateral pedal edema. Which of the following sets of findings are most likely present in this patient?

clues.text: worsen with exertion and when lying flat
clues.note: Dyspnea on exertion plus orthopnea indicates elevated left-heart filling pressures (pulmonary congestion) - left ventricular failure.
Anthracyclines (doxorubicin) cause a dose-dependent DILATED cardiomyopathy that can present with heart failure years to decades after exposure.

clues.text: crackles at the lung bases and bilateral pedal edema
clues.note: Pulmonary crackles (left-sided congestion) PLUS peripheral edema (right-sided/systemic congestion) = biventricular failure -> both LVEDP and right atrial pressure are elevated.

whatMatters: Doxorubicin causes DILATED CARDIOMYOPATHY. Reduced contractility raises LV end-diastolic pressure (transmitted back to the lungs -> crackles, orthopnea). Advanced/biventricular failure also elevates RIGHT ATRIAL PRESSURE (volume overload -> pedal edema). Both RAP and LVEDP are INCREASED. Answer D.
strategy: Read the congestion on both sides: pulmonary crackles/orthopnea = high LVEDP; pedal edema = high RAP. Decompensated dilated cardiomyopathy from anthracycline gives elevated pressures on BOTH sides -> increased RAP AND increased LVEDP. Reject any option with decreased/normal RAP (A, B, F) - overt volume overload makes RAP invariably elevated - and options with decreased LVEDP (A, C), which contradict pulmonary congestion.

options.text: Right atrial pressure decreased, LV end-diastolic pressure decreased
Right atrial pressure decreased, LV end-diastolic pressure increased
Right atrial pressure increased, LV end-diastolic pressure decreased
Right atrial pressure increased, LV end-diastolic pressure increased
Right atrial pressure increased, LV end-diastolic pressure no change
Right atrial pressure no change, LV end-diastolic pressure increased

eliminations.label: Both decreased - volume depletion, not failure
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: low RAP and low LVEDP. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this pattern is intravascular volume DEPLETION; it cannot explain pulmonary crackles and peripheral edema. ✅ Correct if: hypovolemia/hemorrhage.

eliminations.label: Low RAP, high LVEDP - early isolated left failure
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: elevated left-sided pressure with normal/low right-sided pressure (early left heart failure). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: once overt volume overload with PERIPHERAL EDEMA develops, RAP is invariably elevated. ✅ Correct if: early left-sided failure BEFORE systemic congestion.

eliminations.label: High RAP, low LVEDP - isolated right failure
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: elevated right-sided pressure with low left-sided pressure (e.g., pulmonary hypertension/cor pulmonale). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the patient has pulmonary crackles/orthopnea indicating HIGH LVEDP. ✅ Correct if: right heart failure from lung disease without left-sided disease.

eliminations.label: High RAP, unchanged LVEDP - contradicts crackles
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: elevated right-sided pressure with normal left-sided pressure. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: crackles and orthopnea require an ELEVATED LVEDP, not an unchanged one. ✅ Correct if: isolated right-sided overload without pulmonary congestion.

eliminations.label: Unchanged RAP, high LVEDP - ignores edema
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: normal right-sided pressure with elevated left-sided pressure. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: bilateral PEDAL EDEMA signals systemic venous congestion, so RAP must be elevated, not unchanged. ✅ Correct if: pure left-sided failure before systemic congestion develops.

reasoning: Reduced LV contractility raises LVEDP, transmitted back to the lungs (crackles, orthopnea)
Advanced/biventricular failure and volume overload raise right atrial pressure (pedal edema)
-> both RAP and LVEDP are increased; answer D
mechanism: ANTHRACYCLINE chemotherapeutics (e.g., DOXORUBICIN) cause a dose-dependent, often DELAYED DILATED CARDIOMYOPATHY through free-radical-mediated myocyte injury; heart failure can appear years to decades after treatment. Dilated cardiomyopathy impairs systolic contractile function; the LV dilates and, despite Frank-Starling and eccentric hypertrophy compensation, wall stress ultimately produces reduced cardiac output and an ELEVATED LV END-DIASTOLIC PRESSURE (LVEDP). Elevated LVEDP is transmitted backward to the pulmonary veins and capillaries, causing pulmonary congestion (crackles, orthopnea, exertional dyspnea). In advanced disease, RIGHT ATRIAL PRESSURE (which reflects central venous pressure) is also ELEVATED - both from backward transmission of high left-sided pressures causing secondary right-heart failure and because the cardiotoxic insult often directly affects the right ventricle - producing systemic venous congestion with peripheral (pedal) edema. Thus the patient has biventricular failure with BOTH RAP and LVEDP increased. Patterns with a low/normal RAP ignore the overt volume overload, and a low LVEDP contradicts the pulmonary findings.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid CV > dilated cardiomyopathy: causes include anthracyclines (doxorubicin, dose-dependent, delayed); systolic dysfunction -> elevated LVEDP (pulmonary congestion) and elevated RAP/CVP (systemic congestion) in biventricular failure.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Crackles/orthopnea = high LVEDP; pedal edema = high RAP; both elevated in decompensated HF.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on dilated cardiomyopathy, LVEDP, right atrial/central venous pressure, orthopnea, or anthracycline toxicity? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Any low/normal RAP ignores the edema; any low LVEDP ignores the pulmonary crackles.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: doxorubicin -> dilated cardiomyopathy; decompensated HF -> increased RAP AND increased LVEDP.

keywords.back: Elevated right atrial / central venous pressure

firstAid.detail: CV: anthracycline toxicity -> systolic failure; high LVEDP + high RAP.
CV > left congestion = LVEDP; systemic congestion = RAP.
Onc/CV > free-radical myocyte injury; dexrazoxane protection.

memoryHook: Doxorubicin's late gift is a floppy dilated heart - fluid backs up behind BOTH ventricles, so lungs crackle (LVEDP up) and ankles swell (RAP up).
